title: AI Stocks Surge as SpaceX Boosts Dow Jones Futures; Tesla, Meta Set to Follow】
body:
Wall Street opened higher on Tuesday as AI‑related equities surged after SpaceX disclosed a dramatic uptick in demand for its artificial‑intelligence compute hardware and hinted at a possible partnership with Tesla. The news sent Dow Jones futures up around 0.6%, while shares of AI‑focused chipmaker Supermicro jumped more than 9% in pre‑market trading. Tech giants Tesla and Meta Platforms also rose on the back of speculation that the automaker could become a strategic partner in SpaceX’s burgeoning AI initiatives.

SpaceX’s latest earnings briefing revealed that its internal AI compute division, which builds custom‑designed servers for training large language models, has seen “exponential” growth in order volume over the past quarter. The company, long known for its reusable rockets, has been quietly expanding into the high‑performance computing market to support its own satellite‑based AI services and to sell excess capacity to third‑party developers. Analysts estimate that the new revenue stream could add as much as $1.2 billion to SpaceX’s top line by the end of 2027, a figure that would markedly improve the firm’s cash flow and fund further expansion of its Starlink constellation.

The prospect of a Tesla‑SpaceX collaboration amplified investor enthusiasm. Sources close to the two firms suggest that Tesla’s expertise in silicon‑based AI chips and its massive data collection from autonomous‑driving fleets could complement SpaceX’s compute platform, creating a vertically integrated solution for training and deploying next‑generation models at scale. While no formal agreement has been announced, the mere possibility of a joint venture has been enough to lift Tesla shares by roughly 2% in after‑hours trading, as investors anticipate synergies that could lower the cost of AI training and accelerate product rollouts across both companies.

Supermicro, a leading provider of high‑density server and storage solutions, benefited directly from the spillover effect. The company’s stock climbed 9.3% after it disclosed a new partnership with SpaceX to supply rack‑mount servers optimized for the aerospace firm’s AI workloads. The deal underscores a broader trend of traditional hardware manufacturers pivoting toward AI‑centric product lines, as demand for specialized compute infrastructure outpaces the capacity of conventional data centers. Industry observers note that Supermicro’s earnings guidance for the next fiscal year now reflects a 15% increase in AI‑related revenue, positioning it as a key beneficiary of the sector’s rapid expansion.

Meta Platforms also saw a modest gain, up about 1.4%, after the social‑media giant announced it is evaluating a strategic alliance with SpaceX to leverage the latter’s low‑latency satellite network for delivering AI‑enhanced services in underserved regions. The move could help Meta extend the reach of its generative‑AI tools, such as the newly launched LLaMA‑2 models, to markets where terrestrial broadband remains scarce. Although the partnership is still in exploratory stages, analysts argue that the combination of SpaceX’s global connectivity and Meta’s AI expertise could create a competitive edge in the race to dominate the next wave of immersive, AI‑driven experiences.

The rally in AI‑related stocks comes at a time when the broader market remains cautious about inflationary pressures and potential interest‑rate hikes. Yet the sector’s resilience suggests that investors are increasingly treating AI as a distinct growth engine, capable of delivering outsized returns independent of macro‑economic headwinds. With major players like SpaceX, Tesla, Supermicro and Meta all signaling deeper collaboration, the ecosystem surrounding AI compute is likely to tighten, driving further consolidation and innovation.

Looking ahead, market participants will be watching for concrete details on any formal agreements between SpaceX and Tesla, as well as the rollout timeline for SpaceX’s commercial AI compute services. If the partnerships materialize as expected, they could accelerate the deployment of large‑scale models across industries, from autonomous transportation to real‑time satellite analytics, and cement the United States’ leadership in the AI hardware race. For now, the bullish sentiment in AI equities appears poised to sustain momentum, with the potential to reshape investment strategies across the technology sector.
